alignments.note: Quantifying construct noun `כֹּל` rendered by the single word *everything*, which carries the quantification and the generic the ASV builds it on; rule 19's *of* does not arise because the ASV writes no relational word between the two nouns.
Article morpheme with no written *the*; the phrase's determination is carried inside `כֹּל`'s *everything*, so the article is unrepresented under rules 15 and 29.

A supplied relative and a supplied verb of having, standing together and composing the single office of making the Hebrew nominal phrase into a relative clause; one `added` unit under rule 2, headed on *hath*, exactly as `נָצְרוּ דָעַת` → *him that hath knowledge* is. No `הָיָה`, existential particle, possessive preposition, suffix or noun of possession stands in the clause for rule 43 to place the *hath* on.

Jussive rendered by the volitive frame *Let ... praise*; the framing word joins the verb's unit under rule 17 and the unit heads on its lexical predicate, discontinuous under rule 25 around the subject phrase.
The divine name; the 'Hebrew Jah' margin was read and set aside under rule 38.
Imperative with its supplied subject pronoun under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb.
The divine name; the 'Hebrew Hallelujah' margin was read and set aside under rule 38.

review_notes: *that hath* is kept as one `added` unit rather than split word by word, since its two words stand together and do one office and no source morpheme owns either; rule 2 states this expressly for the same construction.
The article on `נְשָׁמָה` is unrepresented because the ASV writes no separate determiner for it: *everything* is `כֹּל`'s own word.
Both marginal glosses are corroborative only and decide nothing, by rule 38.
